# Account service

Arcane accounts use Supabase Auth for verified identity and Stripe for hosted payment entry. These service integrations require deployment configuration; local code and fixture checks do not establish live sign-in or payment acceptance.

The account storage layer encrypts browser session payloads and private identity fields using AES-256-GCM with purpose and record identity bound as authenticated data. Browser identifiers are random and only keyed hashes are stored. Session writes use version checks, absolute expiry and explicit deletion. Encryption keys must be independent, randomly generated server secrets and kept outside source control. A missing or changed key must not silently discard existing records.

The identity adapter authenticates the exact access token through Supabase's `GET /user` before using its subject, issuer, audience, expiry or assurance claims. Email must be verified. User-editable metadata does not grant an admin role. Provider response bodies, passwords and tokens must never enter application logs or public error messages.

The same-origin `/account` page supports email/password registration and login, email verification and recovery, Google and Apple with PKCE, and optional authenticator two-step verification. The server enforces enrolled factors before device approval, checkout or access to balances. The owner must enroll an authenticator; administration requires a second-factor check within the last 15 minutes. Owner access is bootstrapped once from private deployment configuration after verified email and MFA, then bound to the provider's stable subject. User-editable provider metadata never grants a role. The repository contains no owner email or pre-authorized public account.

Browser sessions use opaque HttpOnly cookies, Secure with the `__Host-` prefix on HTTPS, SameSite=Lax, exact-origin checks and a separate CSRF token. Provider access and refresh tokens stay encrypted on the server. Login and factor verification rotate the browser session. Password changes rotate the current session and revoke other Arcane browser and native sessions. Anonymous sessions expire after 15 minutes; signed-in browser and native account sessions have a 30-day absolute expiry. Transient provider failures preserve the existing browser session instead of clearing its cookie. Local logout remains available during an upstream outage. Native device approval expires after five minutes and can only approve the account authenticated in the browser. Legacy bearer records do not bypass managed-account checks.

The `/admin` panel lists accounts, balances, security status and recent audit events. The owner can suspend, restore or revoke member sessions. The panel cannot change owner access or grant funds. Billing Checkout and customer-portal sessions use server-owned account and customer identifiers; browser-submitted email or customer overrides are ignored. Only verified, idempotent payment webhooks grant purchases.

Account encryption uses a `v2` envelope bound to the provider origin as well as the purpose and record identity. Unsupported envelopes, modified ciphertext, stale writes and a wrong key fail without deleting the stored records. Keep `ACCOUNTS_SESSION_KEY`, `AUTH_SECRET`, the provider origin and the persistent database stable across deployments. Back them up separately with restricted access; changing them is an explicit migration or revocation operation, not an app update. Legacy development email-link rows and upstream provider/payment records have their own retention requirements; field encryption does not encrypt the entire SQLite file.

Verification covers real loopback HTTP and SQLite plus an isolated Edge browser, with identity and payment providers explicitly mocked. Cases cover session persistence and refresh, CSRF, PKCE replay, authenticator enrollment and verification, native approval/expiry, owner authorization, suspension, account rate limits and payment ownership/destinations. CI runs service type checking and regression tests on both operating systems and the browser case on Windows. These checks do not establish live provider acceptance.

Before public launch, configure the HTTPS domain, Supabase project, verified-email delivery, Google and Apple registrations, TOTP and an authenticated account-recovery procedure. Test signup, recovery and social callbacks on the real domain. Configure Stripe test products, signed webhooks and its customer portal, then validate payments end to end in test mode. Catalog prices remain placeholders until approved; do not create live charges from them. No production provider credentials or deployment have been provisioned by this implementation.

Use TLS, encrypted production storage and backups, restricted service credentials and audited access. Encryption protects specific boundaries; it is not a guarantee against every possible data leak.

References: [Supabase Auth API](https://github.com/supabase/auth/blob/master/openapi.yaml), [MFA enforcement](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa), [server-validated users](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getuser), [Stripe Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout).
